author: TheMovieSearch R
content:
Ne Zha (2019) is a wildly imaginative and energetic animated film that fully earns its reputation. After seeing the sequel, going back to the original feels essential, and it absolutely holds up on its own. The story blends mythology, humor, action, and emotion in a way that feels bold and confident from start to finish.

Even when some of the mythological details feel dense or unfamiliar, the direction and pacing keep you grounded. You always understand the emotional core of the story: a child born with a cursed destiny who refuses to accept the role the world assigns him. That theme of defying fate gives the film real heart.

The animation is vibrant, expressive, and packed with kinetic action, while the character work makes Ne Zha instantly memorable. It’s funny, chaotic, heartfelt, and surprisingly moving. This isn’t just a strong animated film, it’s the foundation of a franchise with lasting impact. Creative, emotional, and highly rewatchable.

author: Jay W
content:
This movie rocks a runtime of 1 hour 50 minutes, which is fairly long for an animated movie. Of these 110 minutes there is not a single one that is boring. This is both the movie's greatest strength, and ironically its biggest weakness.

I watched this movie with a 4-year old and a 6-year old, and this movie captivated them for the entire runtime. These kids don't have the best of attention spans, but during this film they were never bored. They may have been completely lost about the plot, but they were always entertained.

This leads to how this pacing is a problem. There is so much that happens in this movie, it could have probably been a TV series. As somebody described the premise of the movie, I thought they were telling me the whole story. But no, what they were describing was just the first 4 minutes of the story.

It is a retelling of a classic Chinese tale, I'm sure those familiar with the original will be able to follow the movie much better. I like a lot of the ideas the movie explores. There's a bit of nature vs. Nurture debate. The main character, NeZha, gets a reputation of being a monstrous child. The movie proposes the question of whether the child earned this dubious honor, or did the society create this monster.

The movie unfortunately fumbles these themes in execution. NeZha acts too much like the victim, not taking responsibility for all the terrible things he does. And the parents don't do much in raising him, kind of underplaying the nature vs. Nurture idea. I do enjoy that parents aren't dead or villainized, which seem to be the only two settings for parents in kids' movies.

The movie has great animation for the many action scenes. It is hit and miss with its humor. Some characters are over reliant on one joke that is repeated too often. But as a whole, I think the good jokes outweigh the bad, including one mid-credit scene that got a huge laugh out of me.

The movie is undeniably creative and has a lot of energy. There may be a lot covered in this review, but there is a lot covered in this movie. I say give it a watch, you'll nezha regret it.

On August 31, 2019, "Ne Zha" made the second largest box-office record of Chinese movies. So you may wonder, what makes "Ne Zha" so popular?
"Ne Zha" which was a new released animated movie last summer based on a chinese legendary mythical figure called "Nezha" directed and written by Jiaozi. It is still on trends because of its interesting acting styles and meaningful content. As soon as I saw it, I became a fan of this movie and even watched it twice later.  
Nezha was chosen to be a reincarnation of a good spirit. However, unfortunately it was replaced with the evilest spirit when he was born. He showed his stubborn and mischievous nature which made the villagers panic. In the process of his growing up, the villagers had always treated him with prejudice and fear, no matter what he thought or did. The prejudice was that monsters in people's hearts can cover their eyes and can't see the truth. Finally, until Nezha tried his best to save the villagers, they really let go of their prejudices and accepted him.
The reason why I like it is because it gives us some positive energy about life. Nezha said: "My destiny isn't written in the stars, but held in my hands." You know, maybe we all have our own destinies. However, there are still some parts of our lives that can be changed to be good if our minds are set to be so. So who are you, do you have the final say? We are constantly defined by various occasions and needs. Regarding the truth about ourselves, sometimes we have no say in ourselves. Just like the protagonist Meursault in "The Outsider "by the existentialist master Camus, he has no right to speak on the truth of the case he is involved in. This world is sometimes so ridiculous, and many of us in it just endure silently. Therefore, the explosive moment of "Nezha" must arouse the blood and passion in the hearts of the audience. We need Nezha, even if it's just in the movie.
The film retains the essence of Chinese traditional culture, good visual effects; the other is the modernity and sense of humor in character shaping and language style. There is also an ugly side in the film. Compared to the truth, many people are more willing to believe in hearsay and then look at people with colored glasses. Moreover, the writer clearly used "Ao Bing" as a contrast to Nezha, highlighting that whether a man or a devil is an independent choice, rather than a subject that is destined by nature.
Generally speaking, I take the view that this Chinese animation is of good quality and worth watching. The final product is fascinating and stunning with great humor, deep emotion, exciting action.
My fav Chinese animated film.

The movie of Nezha is set in a Mythical world in China. There is a powerful orb that absorbs all energy, which was meant to be destroyed by Taiyi and Shen, two immortals with great powers. It is known as the Chaos Pearl. The Chaos Pearl is divided into two opposite orbs by Yuan Shi (the primordial lord of heaven) the Spirit Pearl and the Demon Orb. Casting a spell of destruction on the Demon Orb to be destroyed in three years so that it doesn't destroy the world.  Yuan Shi gives the order to Taiyi to take the spirit pearl so that it can be born into a human. The spirit pearl was supposed to be born as Nezha however due to Shen switching the orbs a young boy is birthed from the Demon Orb whose demonic nature is apparent. 
As a young boy, Nezha is loved by his parents who lied to him to tame his demonic nature. He is trained by Taiyi to become a demon hunter and is told that he was born from the Spirit Pearl. Becoming impatient he escapes to hunt demons where he meets Ao Bing (also trained to hunt demons)  who was born from the spirit pearl as a dragon and was educated rigorously to become a demon hunter and to beware of humans. They fight together the demon however Ao Bing loses, and Nezha ends up rescuing him. The villagers however misinterpret the situation and blame all the destruction on Nezha due to his demonic nature. Nezha and Ao Bing become friends.
However Nezhas's third birthday is coming, his parents throw him a birthday party and force the town to come. Shen visits Nezha before the party and tells him that he has lied to his whole life and that he was born of the demon orb. Nezha feels betrayed and unleashes his demonic powers destroying everything and almost killing his dad however he leaves to await his fate. 
Shen knows that if  Yuan Shi finds out the truth about what had happened. Tat all of the dragon race will be condemned. So Ao bing decides to use his powers to destroy Nezha's village to erase any evidence of the events. Nezha is shown through a vision that his dad had been trying to find a way to remove the curse. In which he takes the curse upon himself so that Nezha could live. Because of this Nezha returns to his village to stop Ao Bing from destroying his village. He defeats Ao bing but spares him. When lighting comes to kill him he surrenders to his fate. However, Ao bing joins him in taking the hit of the lighting. Because of them joining the Chaos Pearl is once again united and can absorb the full hit of the lighting. Taiyi makes it possible for their spirits to survive. 
This story plays the themes of nature vs. nurture and choice. Even though Nezha was naturally born with a demonic spirit, didn't have many friends, and was feared and hated by his village, he was raised by good parents who loved him, taught him to control himself, and was told that he was born from the spirit pearl. So when Nezha was growing up, he had a pretty positive paradigm about himself, which led him to be able to control his demonic nature and be good. On the other, hand, we see Ao Bing being born from the spirit pearl he was told that he was going to be great, he did however have a rougher upbringing being raised by the king of the dragons and trained by Shen, and like a dragon, he was a hated creature by humans, but he was loved by his kin.
When the time comes for them to know, and be faced by who they are. They have the choice to be what their destinies told them to be, or who they were raised to. Having to choose to act upon their natures, what they were told their whole life to be, or choose between good and bad.
Nezha decides to act for himself and not let his nature control him, he decides to defend his family, his village, and what is right. What is interesting for me is not Nezha's struggle with choice, but it is Ao Bings. He was way more likely to be good since he was born from the Spirit Pearl, but because of the way he was nurtured to protect his kin he struggles with the choice of helping Nezha save his village or helping Shen. However, in the end, he helps Nezha and also helps Nezha's life as a spirit by uniting their powers. Overall I love this movie because of the character development presented and the message of us choosing to act and not be acted upon. It is also light-hearted and a perfect family night movie. The final rating would be 5 stars!

Nezha is one of the most popular and well-known mythical characters in China. Nezha appear in many myths. There are various versions of Nezha's story, and it has been adapted many times in animation and movies. But this adaptation is revolutionary.

In the original myths, Nezha is a good boy, but the plot is way more violent. In the myths, Nezha is human baby borne with divine power. His father is indifferent and strict with him. One day, Hezhan caught the Dragon Prince killing children, and then he killed the Dragon Prince (cruelly skinned the young dragon alive). When Dragon King found out, it came to Nezha's revenge. The Dragon King wanted to flood Nezha's hometown with seawater. To protect the village, Nezha committed suicide in front of the Dragon King and his parents. Later, Nezha was resurrected in the lotus and became a God. Then Nazhe destroyed the dragon palace, caught the Dragon King, and became one of the Gods of War. In other versions, Nezha killed a total of 9 dragons.

Comparing to the original myth, this movie is chill and light hearted in a good way. The rebellious character of Nezha is fresh and interesting to watch. This story emphasis on the lesson of "choosing your own path", where the original version is more about "unconditional self-sacrifice" and "孝道(obedience towards elder family members)". The revised story in the film is more in line with modern values ​​than the original myths.

author: matthias s
content:
**Ne Zha 2 – ★★★½**

I’ll admit, I found the first *Ne Zha* kinda mediocre, but curiosity got the better of me—and wow, this sequel really goes for it. It’s no surprise it broke the box office: the humor actually lands, the animation is stunning, and some scenes are jaw-dropping in scale and detail. There’s a surprising amount of depth too, balancing goofy jokes with dark, emotional stakes. It’s definitely a big step up from the first one.

That said, the story is a bit of a beautiful mess. Half the time I was asking, “Wait, who’s that again?” or “Why is this happening?” It’s way too long and kinda lost me in the middle, which is a shame because the final act is pure visual perfection. I totally get the hype—it’s ambitious, bold, and often breathtaking—but I just wasn’t as swept up in it as I hoped to be.

That's another really cool thing about this movie: most of the main characters have a duality between "good" and "evil"/ "light" and "dark" sides. 

I really like or at least was intrigued by all the characters. Of course I probably like the main characters the most, and I thought their romance was done pretty well, but I also really liked the fox demon that ran the Precious Jade shop. They did a fantastic job of making her both really cool and fun and yet at the same time, because of her fox side, she was also very manipulative and a little scary. The scenes in her workshop are particularly awesome with how whimsical everything feels and yet there's the feeling that these things are very powerful and could easily ruin you. The way the characters and the items flying around the room move in these scenes on top of what is being said and how bright and colorful everything is— it all works together so well. On that note, I also think all the music pairs really well with their scenes. 

The only minor things that I don't  quite love about the movie are 1. There are a couple times where it feels like a scene is cut out and the two surrounding scenes get spliced together without any or much transition which is a little confusing. 2.
